new_findings.title: CryptoBridge.getLocalStateStatus references API-33-only KeyStoreException with minSdk=26
new_findings.notes: class=RUNTIME_DEFECT; explanation=CryptoBridge.getLocalStateStatus() directly references android.security.KeyStoreException in a catch block, but that class exists only from API 33. With minSdk=26, any device on API 26-32 that reaches this path will crash with NoClassDefFoundError before LocalStateStatus can be returned. The path is reachable from RegistrationOrchestrator.uploadPublicIdentity() via CryptoBridgeLocalE2eeIdentityStep.ensurePublicIdentityMaterial().; fix=Guard the KeyStoreException branch with Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU, or catch a common base and rethrow/dispatch without literal class reference; preserve AEADBadTagException and UnrecoverableKeyException handling.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-ANDROID-SEC/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=android-emulator-api-26-32 crash. Class A foundation blocker.

new_findings.title: Unsafe concurrent &mut access to native Identity/Session handles
new_findings.notes: class=MEMORY_SAFETY; explanation=The Rust JNI bridge tracks active handles in a Mutex<HashSet>, but the Identity and Session objects themselves are not serialized. cryptoGenerateOneTimeKeys takes &mut Identity while cryptoGetOneTimeKey / oneTimeKeysCount take &Identity on the same handle. cryptoCreateInboundSession also takes &mut Identity. The current registration path invokes these sequentially on one thread, so the race is latent; any future concurrent Product caller (coroutine/Executor/lifecycle) creates a data race and undefined behavior in the Rust layer.; fix=Introduce a per-handle lock in Rust (or at the CryptoBridge layer) so that all Identity/Session operations on the same handle are mutually exclusive; document the thread-safety contract.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-CRYPTO/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=YES (concurrency boundary); systemic_reaudit=concurrency-race. Class A foundation blocker.

new_findings.title: Device Auth key not re-verified before markArmed / commit
new_findings.notes: class=STATE_MACHINE; explanation=RegistrationOrchestrator stores the deviceAuthJwkThumbprint at registerDeviceAuth() and reuses it in commit() without re-checking that the Device Auth key is still present or that the thumbprint matches the current key. If the platform invalidates the key (or a new key is created by an external call before markArmed), commit() will call markArmed(), markBound() and clear the session, leaving the installation bound to a key the device no longer has. The commitRegistration API takes no new Device Auth proof, so the client cannot demonstrate possession at this step.; fix=Re-verify DeviceAuth key presence and thumbprint equality before markArmed() in commit(); fail closed if the key is missing or the thumbprint does not match the stored value. If the B-004 commit API requires a fresh proof, add a signing step.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-B002/B003/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=registration-arming. Class A foundation blocker.

new_findings.title: E2EE identity persisted before one-time keys generated; OTK private state never re-serialized
new_findings.notes: class=DATA_INCONSISTENCY; explanation=createAndPersistFirstIdentity() serializes and writes anox_identity.enc with zero one-time keys. CryptoBridgeLocalE2eeIdentityStep.ensurePublicIdentityMaterial() then calls generateOneTimeKeys() and getOneTimeKey() on the in-memory identity and uploads the public OTKs, but never calls saveIdentity() to persist the updated identity. A crash or process restart after upload leaves the server with a set of public OTKs whose private counterparts were never durably serialized; on retry the identity is loaded from the old file, a new random set of OTKs is generated and uploaded, and the client can no longer decrypt messages targeting the first set.; fix=Generate OTKs before the first serialization and persist the identity with the OTKs, or call saveIdentity() after OTK generation and before/after upload. Mark OTKs as published only after an authoritative server ACK.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-CRYPTO/B003/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=crash-consistency-otk. Class A foundation blocker.

new_findings.title: CommitArmed registration session and DeviceAuthBindingStore armed flag can diverge
new_findings.notes: class=STATE_MACHINE; explanation=commit() first saves RegistrationState.CommitArmed, then calls deviceAuthBindingStore.markArmed(). If markArmed() throws, failStep() does not overwrite the durable session (it only overwrites NotStarted/Failed). On resume, currentState() is CommitArmed but isArmed() is false, so expiredOrNull() is not short-circuited at line 233. Once the grant TTL expires, the session is downgraded to Expired, sessionStore.save(Expired) is called, canStartNew() becomes true, and a new registration can begin while anox_identity.enc from the old transaction persists.; fix=On resuming a CommitArmed state, detect !isArmed() and re-arm (or fail closed with a reason that does not permit expiry downgrade) before evaluating grant expiry. Do not allow a durable CommitArmed session to become Expired.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-B002/B003/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=state-machine-divergence. Class A foundation blocker.

new_findings.title: Native Identity handles created by registration path are not destroyed
new_findings.notes: class=RESOURCE_LEAK; explanation=CryptoBridgeLocalE2eeIdentityStep.resolveIdentityHandle() and CryptoBridge.createAndPersistFirstIdentity() create a Rust Identity, return the jlong handle, and never call CryptoNative.cryptoDestroyIdentity(). The Rust Identity remains in ACTIVE_IDENTITIES and leaks its heap allocation. In the current single-path first-run flow this does not multiply in one process, but any repeated call to getLocalStateStatus() / ensurePublicIdentityMaterial() creates additional in-memory copies of the same identity; over the app lifetime this can cause native memory pressure.; fix=Hold a single canonical Identity handle in CryptoBridge (e.g., cached under cryptoLock) or use AutoCloseable/Cleaner/finalize to release handles when Kotlin owners are done. Ensure destroyIdentity is called whenever a temporary handle is no longer needed.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-CRYPTO/INTEGRATION; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=handle-lifecycle. Class F non-blocking cleanup.

new_findings.title: UuidV4.parse() does not verify RFC4122 variant
new_findings.notes: class=PARSER_CORRECTNESS; explanation=The KDoc on UuidV4.parse() states it verifies RFC 4122 variant 1, version 4, but the implementation only checks uuid.version() == 4. A UUID with the version 4 bits but a non-RFC4122 variant would be accepted, slightly widening the accepted identifier space beyond the server-issued v4 set. Low security impact because account_id, device_id and registration_id are server-generated.; fix=Also verify uuid.variant() == 2 (RFC4122 variant 1) before returning the parsed UUID.; code_affected=YES; legacy=LEGACY-AUDIT-B003; trust_boundary_change=NO; systemic_reaudit=parser-correctness. Class F non-blocking cleanup.
